result.title: Joint Embedding with Dynamic Integration network (JEDI-net)
result.summary: Deep learning has become the dominant form of machine learning due in part, to its ability to automatically engineer complex meta features from data. However, even deep learning features can perform erratically because of unobserved latent factors. incorporating latent factor information explicitly, can improve performance by letting the model alter its behavior based on such inferred factors. Because neural networks often capture such complexity inherently, external clustering of the original feature space offers limited benefit. clustering observations by feature importance profiles, rather than raw features, offers a principled way to uncover latent structure, since observations with similar importance patterns may share predictive dynamics. In a prior work, Feature Oriented Representation with Clustering and Explanation (FORCE) we showed that this approach measurably improved neural network performance. In this article, we present JEDI-net(Joint Embedding with Dynamic Integration Network) a unified architecture that periodically clusters SHAP values during optimization to identify latent subgroups with similar feature importance patterns, embed their identities directly into the network, allowing predictions to adapt to each observations predictive structure.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 JEDI-net 这一统一架构，在优化过程中周期性对 SHAP 值聚类以发现具有相似特征重要性模式的潜在子群，并把子群身份直接嵌入网络，使预测随每个样本的预测结构自适应调整。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作与视觉/多模态推理无直接关联，但其「按重要性剖面聚类出潜在子群、再动态条件化网络行为」的思路，可能与 LVR 中潜在推理模式的分组抽象、内部状态条件化，以及用贡献归因筛选视觉证据等问题的表述存在概念联系，可供核查。
